title: SWISSto12 Taps DLR for HummingSat Flight Dynamics
html:
Keeping a satellite in the right orbit requires more than propulsion. Precise calculations are needed to determine its position, plan maneuvers, and maintain antenna alignment throughout its operational life. For compact geostationary satellites, these tasks become particularly important when electric propulsion is involved.

Swiss aerospace company SWISSto12 has selected the German Aerospace Center (DLR) as its primary flight dynamics software provider for upcoming HummingSat missions. The agreement, announced on November 18, will see the German Space Operations Center (GSOC) support the company’s geostationary satellite programs.

For eeNews Europe readers, the collaboration is particularly relevant to satellite control systems and Europe’s space industry. It shows how established flight dynamics software can support smaller GEO platforms, where precise orbit management and efficient propulsion are essential to mission performance.

Flight Dynamics for HummingSat Missions

Under the agreement, DLR’s GSOC will provide software covering orbit determination, trajectory prediction, maneuver planning, calibration, and antenna pointing.

The software will also support orbit event management and long-term mission analysis, allowing SWISSto12 to standardize flight dynamics across its HummingSat programs.

One of the main technical challenges involves electric propulsion. Unlike conventional chemical propulsion, electric thrusters typically deliver low thrust over extended periods, making accurate trajectory modeling and maneuver planning particularly important.

The software must also account for electric station-keeping and missions requiring coordinated orbit and attitude control.

By integrating GSOC’s flight dynamics tools into its ground segment architecture, SWISSto12 aims to improve orbital accuracy while reducing operational risks.

European Expertise Behind Satellite Operations

GSOC operates within DLR’s Space Operations and Astronaut Training institute in Oberpfaffenhofen, near Munich.

The center has already supported SWISSto12 with mission analysis across several programs. The new contract extends that relationship to flight dynamics software for upcoming missions.

“The German Space Operations Center has supported SWISSto12 since the early phases of the HummingSat missions,” said Prof. Felix Huber, Director of DLR’s Space Operations and Astronaut Training institute.

According to Huber, the collaboration has also contributed to further development of the software to meet HummingSat’s specific requirements.

For SWISSto12, using a common European flight dynamics solution across its satellite programs could simplify operations and provide a consistent approach to mission planning.

Supporting the Next Generation of GEO Satellites

Founded in 2011, SWISSto12 develops satellite payloads using advanced manufacturing techniques, including 3D printing.

Its HummingSat platform is designed for compact geostationary missions, offering an alternative to larger conventional GEO satellites.

The company is currently delivering seven HummingSat platforms to global operators, alongside payloads for several low Earth orbit constellations.

HummingSat is also an ESA Partnership Project, reflecting the involvement of Europe’s wider space industry in its development.

As SWISSto12 prepares these missions, reliable flight dynamics software will be essential for maintaining orbital positions, planning propulsion maneuvers, and keeping communications payloads accurately pointed throughout their service life.

summary: SWISSto12 selects DLR for HummingSat flight dynamics software, supporting precise orbit control and electric propulsion in GEO missions.
